Hrubieszow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Hrubieszów, Poland

Demolished. Hrubieszów's Jewish cemetery, established either shortly after 1578 or possibly earlier, once covered 3.1 hectares and included a funeral home and an ohel. It was seriously damaged during WWII, its tombstones used for construction, and in 1942–1943 German forces shot about 500 Jews at the cemetery itself and buried them there in mass graves. A group of survivors exhumed and reburied victims from around the town in 1945–1946, gathering surviving tombstones and fencing the site, though it was later neglected and partly overbuilt with warehouses in the 1970s. Since 1990, the cemetery has been regularly maintained and re-fenced, with a second Holocaust memorial and a lapidarium built from 76 recovered matzevot — the oldest dated 1815 — now marking the site, explaining why, despite its official 'demolished' status, its preservation-condition category reads 'fenced and protected' today.
